name: General prohibition / restriction
legal_question: Does the law restrict cross-border transfer of personal data as a default?
in_scope: Default restriction on transferring personal data outside the jurisdiction
Requirement to keep data onshore / locally unless conditions met
Prohibition on sending personal data to foreign recipients
out_of_scope: Government data or national security exclusions applied to public agencies only
Financial/banking secrecy provisions (covered under different pillars)
Technical standards for data centres already established domestically

name: Adequacy standard
legal_question: Can data be transferred to countries with adequate protection?
in_scope: Transfer permitted to countries with comparable or adequate data protection
Whitelist or approved country list for outbound transfers
Adequacy assessment mechanism
out_of_scope: Intra-group data sharing without adequacy assessment

name: Contractual safeguards
legal_question: Are standard contractual clauses or BCRs accepted as transfer mechanisms?
in_scope: SCCs or model clauses explicitly named as transfer mechanism
Binding corporate rules accepted as lawful transfer basis
Contractual obligations on recipient to maintain equivalent protection
out_of_scope: General data processing agreements not related to cross-border transfer

name: Consent exception
legal_question: Can transfer proceed with individual consent?
in_scope: Explicit individual consent as a basis for cross-border transfer
Informed consent allowing overseas data transfer
out_of_scope: Consent for data collection (not specifically for transfer)

name: Other exceptions
legal_question: What other lawful bases permit cross-border transfer beyond consent and adequacy?
in_scope: Transfer necessary for contract performance with the data subject
Transfer for vital interests or life-safety situations
Transfer for legal claims or court proceedings
Public interest exception for transfers

name: Legal basis for processing
legal_question: Does the law require a lawful basis for collecting or processing personal data?
in_scope: Requirement for lawful basis before collecting or processing personal data
Enumeration of lawful bases (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests)
Prohibition on processing without a lawful basis
out_of_scope: Government data or public sector exclusions
Employee data processed under employment law (unless explicitly covered)

name: Purpose limitation
legal_question: Is data restricted to the purpose for which it was collected?
in_scope: Prohibition on using personal data for purposes other than the stated collection purpose
Requirement to disclose purpose at point of collection
Secondary use prohibition unless new consent obtained
out_of_scope: Data retention rules (covered under a separate indicator)

name: Data subject rights
legal_question: Do individuals have rights to access, correct, or delete their personal data?
in_scope: Right to request access to personal data held by an organisation
Right to correct inaccurate or incomplete personal data
Right to withdraw consent and have data deleted or processed no further
Right to data portability (transfer data to another organisation)
out_of_scope: Rights of legal entities (not natural persons)

name: Data breach notification
legal_question: Is there a mandatory data breach notification requirement?
in_scope: Mandatory notification to supervisory authority when a data breach occurs
Notification to affected individuals when breach is likely to cause harm
Specific timeframe for notification (e.g. 72 hours, 3 days)
out_of_scope: Voluntary breach disclosure without legal obligation

name: Enforcement & penalties
legal_question: Is there a supervisory authority and penalty regime for data protection violations?
in_scope: Establishment of a data protection commissioner or supervisory body
Powers of the authority to investigate and enforce
Financial penalties or fines for violations
Criminal offences and imprisonment terms for serious breaches
out_of_scope: Self-regulatory industry bodies without statutory powers
